title: Sex-specific developmental phenotypes and their response to neonatal Dyrk1a reduction in the Ts65Dn Down syndrome mouse model.
abstract: Ts65Dn Down syndrome model pups are trisomic for ~100 Hsa21 orthologs including Dyrk1a, and both sexes show significant DYRK1A overexpression at postnatal day 6 in hippocampus, cortex and cerebellum. The study tested whether normalizing Dyrk1a copy number before P6 would diminish physical and behavioral developmental deficits. At P3-P21, Ts65Dn pups showed sex-specific deficits in physical, motor and behavioral development. Male Dyrk1a-normalized mice showed improved emergence to running at P19, and both sexes showed reduced isolation-induced ultrasonic vocalizations during the second postnatal week. Copy number normalization did not improve all abnormal phenotypes.
